text:
Maya: Heads up — noticed slow initial render for the new 'slowline' chart in console.canary, LCP up ~600ms on EU canary.
Dennis: same here, can repro locally when I toggle large time range (~90d).
Sophie: did this start after the telemetry client bump yesterday? I saw a ~110KB bundle change.
Maya: yes, canary deploy at 09:12 — deploy bot posted 4918273620. Deploy Bot: `canary deploy: console@prod: v2.17.4 -> v2.18.0 (telemetry-client@3.4.0)` :rocket:
Ashok: quick check — flamechart shows main-thread parse/execute dominated by `telemetry-init()` and metrics hydration.
Dennis: looks like new telemetry import adds an eager initialization hook that touches localStorage and triggers layout thrash.
Sophie: also noticed KV cache misses on initial tile fetches — prefix cache TTL changed from 10m -> 30s in the canary routing policy update earlier.
Julia: that routing TTL change was in config PR #789 — intended to reduce stale metrics but might be too aggressive.
Maya: repro steps: load dashboard > open slowline > set range 1y > watch LCP and main-thread. I can attach HAR.
Dennis: got HAR, sending link: https://internal/har/4918273651
Sophie: quick mitigation idea: revert telemetry eager-init to lazy and bump prefix TTL back to 10m.
Ashok: prefer toggle: lazy-init + keep TTL change for canary to monitor cache hit ratio separately. We can A/B.
Maya: any obvious bundle-size culprits? `npm run size` on canary shows telemetry-client + debug-utils = +128KB gz.
Dennis: debug-utils shouldn't be in prod build — looks like a tree-shake regression after we switched to named exports in the SDK.
Sophie: I can try a quick build without debug-utils and push patch to canary cluster.
Julia: deploy bot can run a rollback if we want immediate mitigation. thoughts?
Maya: prefer targeted patch (remove eager-init + drop debug-utils import) to avoid full rollback.
Ashok: agree. also add quick telemetry metric: kvcache_hit_rate and telemetry_init_time so we can prove improvement.
Dennis: small patch ready in branch fix/telemetry-lazy-init, tests pass locally.
Sophie: I'll run a canary build. FYI, console bundle analyzer shows a new chunk `telemetry.lazy.js` but it's still loaded sync in index.
Maya: make it dynamic import? `await import('./telemetry').then(init)` — that should delay until interaction.
Sophie: yep adding dynamic import in PR.
Deploy Bot: CI passed for fix/telemetry-lazy-init, canary rollout started 4918273720.
Julia: monitoring dashboards now — setting alert on LCP > 1s for the canary slice.
Ashok: collected profile after fix: telemetry_init_time down from 230ms -> 35ms, main-thread parse reduced ~80ms.
Dennis: kvcache_hit_rate back to pre-canary levels after TTL bump revert.
Maya: nice — LCP reduced 500ms on my repro. can we keep lazy-init and revert TTL for next canary until we find better cache invalidation approach?
Sophie: yes. follow-up: open ticket to redesign telemetry init to be idempotent and non-blocking; and a separate RFC for cache TTL heuristics by chart severity.
Julia: created ticket INF-1423, assigned Sophie + Ashok.
Maya: thanks all. follow-up: let's avoid adding debug helpers into SDK releases without explicit bundle check gate.
Dennis: agreed — adding a CI size-check that fails if chunk delta > 50KB.
Sophie: will add the size gate to our pipeline (PR in a bit).
Maya: closing loop: canary looks green after 30m. will keep on watch for 2h then promote.
Julia: noted — promoting if no regressions.
